name: list_tags
title: List assignable tags
description:
The active workspace tag catalog, in deterministic name order. Each entry carries the stable canonical `id` documents store and its current display `name`. Retired entries are absent here but remain visible, marked retired, on documents that still carry them. MCP cannot curate this catalog.

`complete` says whether this is the whole workspace vocabulary. It is false while a configured hub has not delivered the catalog room to this replica: what is listed is then a local copy that may be missing curated entries, and a tag value this replica has never seen is refused rather than assigned. `hub` says where that connection stands.

name: create_doc
title: Create a document

title.description: Display title; required except on a successor. Identity is the document's UUID, never this. A decision topic has one title, stored on its first record, naming the question rather than the answer. A rename through any record renames the topic. Successors take the topic's title; omit title or supply that same title. For decision answers, see lifecycle's Decision answers and topics section. Answer blocks are distinct from recorded answer: {who, when, where}.

description.description: Agent-facing description used to choose whether to open the document.

tldr.description: One or two sentences of plain English for a person opening a regular document. At most 300 characters; null clears it. Decisions have no TL;DR.

when.description: When the person gave the answer, preferably an ISO date-time.

where.description: Where the answer was given, such as a conversation or review URL.

answer.description: Record a person's answer, not the agent's own approval. MCP does not verify its provenance.

kind.description: The document's record kind. Omit it for an ordinary working document.

status.description: The recorded lifecycle state. Its kind owns the legal values.

related.description: Live, locally readable regular document UUID this decision relates to. Fixed at creation; omitted successors inherit their predecessor's page. Accepted only with `kind: decision`.

discussion.description: Live, locally readable regular document UUID holding this record's RFC discussion. Accepted only with `kind: decision`; never inherited. Correct or clear with set_metadata only while open; fixed after leaving open. Does not create or tag a document.

supersedes.description: Earlier decision UUID this new decision replaces. Immutable and accepted only with `kind: decision`.

text.description: Block text. A table takes exactly one GFM table with inline Markdown cell formatting; alignment is not stored. A card takes the content between exact :::card and ::: lines: lowercase label, title and footer at most once, a required nonempty title, any number of button lines, then a blank line and optional prose body. Prose header values are one-line inline Markdown, not YAML; quotes stay literal. Each button has one [Text](destination) link: nonempty plain text and an https URL or claude://code/new, claude-cli://open or codex://new, alone or with ?query. At most one style (outline/filled) and color (neutral/blue/green/violet) may follow in either order; defaults are outline neutral. Invalid buttons, other trailing text, unknown, duplicate prose or non-key headers refuse with invalid_card. Prose parts support code, bold, italic, strike, external and document links. Export orders label, title, footer, then buttons in authored order, writes style before color and omits default words. Empty prose keys are omitted, prose header newlines fold to spaces, and prose lines starting ::: are escaped. Figma takes the content between :::figma and :::; required url, optional literal plain one-line title and whole-pixel height 240–960 (default 480), then a blank line and optional caption with the same inline marks. Keys are lowercase, each at most once. Only https figma.com/www.figma.com links to design, file, proto, board, slides or community/file are accepted, with a key/id and optional name; saving keeps those path parts and node-id, starting-point-node-id and version-id on https://www.figma.com, dropping other query fields and fragments. Invalid content refuses with invalid_figma and writes nothing; figma blocks take figma.com links only; use a plain link for other sites. get_doc returns canonical text and read-only figma kind, file, optional fileName and node. Source blocks remain literal text.

language.description: Code language, e.g. "ts". Code blocks only.

list.description: List style. List items only; omitted means bullet.

indent.description: List depth, an integer from 0 to 3. List items only; omitted means 0.

inline.description:
Formatted content for a PROSE block (paragraph, heading, list-item, quote), as runs of equally-marked text: `[{text, marks}]`, where marks are `bold`, `italic`, `strike`, `inlineCode`, `link` (an external http(s) URL) and `docLink` (another document's UUID — the inline way to cite one). When present it REPLACES `text`, so the run texts joined together are the block's text. Code, terminal and chart hold source text and ignore it; tables, cards and figma also ignore it and read inline Markdown through `text`: exactly one GFM table or the content between :::card/:::figma and :::.

A `docLink` run with an EMPTY `text` is filled in for you with the target's current title, so `{text: "", marks: {docLink: "<uuid>"}}` is how you cite a document without looking its title up first. A target this replica's directory has never heard of fails the call with `doclink_target_not_known_locally` and writes nothing; an archived target is fine.

sidebar.description: Optional sidebar placement. Omitted, the document is created unpinned — alive and reachable, simply not an entry point.

id.description: An EXISTING group's id, as get_sidebar returns it. Never a name: an unknown id fails the call.

position.description: Position in the group, clamped into range. Omitted means last.

oneOf.title: A decision document (`kind: decision`). A decision topic has one title, stored on its first record, naming the question rather than the answer. A rename through any record renames the topic. Successors take the topic's title; omit title or supply that same title. For decision answers, see lifecycle's Decision answers and topics section. Answer blocks are distinct from recorded answer: {who, when, where}.

description:
Create doc/stub; optional blocks/regular-page TL;DR. Require nonblank description; title is required except for successors. A decision topic has one title stored on its first record. Renaming any record renames the topic. Successors inherit it: omit title or supply the same title; another refuses. List-item seeds: bullet/ordered list, integer indent 0–3 (defaults bullet/0). Active tags by id/name (case ignored); unknown/retired refuse. Kind defaults first status; invalid pairs refuse. Decision topics/answers: consult get_help({topic: "lifecycle"}), including When to create a decision record and Decision answers and topics. Links/GitHub references: markdown. Open/decided only; deciding needs supported nonblank answer blocks, no TL;DR/data; decided successors require recorded human answer. related: live readable regular page; inherited unless supplied. supersedes: hydrated decision in live topic. Targets validated pre-write. discussion: live, readable regular RFC UUID; reuse/create first. Never inherited; set_metadata corrects/clears while open, then fixed. RFC/page untouched. Separate from curated links/recorded answer. Sidebar: get_sidebar group id; invalid = group_not_found, no creation; omit = unpinned. Independent rooms: persistence_failed: uuid, completed/failed, rolledBack: false, duplicate-safe recovery. answerPreview: first answer paragraph/list. Page get_doc: related/linked topics.

name: get_doc
title: Read a document
description:
Read metadata, blocks/rev and threads; page rev equals the web status row's revision. Regular pages return related then linked decision topics; code_check is [] or latest repository/commit/checked_at/result plus recorded rev/paths when known; paths are hints, not complete dependencies. Results: matches (agrees), ahead (intentionally undelivered), drift (unintended disagreement). Content edits preserve checks; decisions omit them. Decision discussion: RFC UUID/null, apart from curated links and recorded answer. Decisions have no TL;DR (tldr: null); entries cache discussion and answerPreview (first paragraph/list, max 300 chars), absent if unknown. Unset description/TL;DR: null; data lists collections/counts for get_data. Tables: canonical GFM. Cards: canonical content with ordered button lines after footer; see get_help for link/style/color syntax. Figma: :::figma content, no delimiters, normalized url, optional plain title/height, blank line, marked caption; read-only kind (frame/file/prototype/board/slides/community file), file, optional decoded fileName (dashes as spaces), node (12:345). Tables/cards/Figma rev includes formatting and button values/order; other rev ignores marks. Prose doc_links has ranges; containers have none. Card thread ranges name part; Figma uses caption offsets. No Figma request; eligible guidance counts toward this process's briefing.

name: get_data
title: Read document data

collection.description: Collection name; omit for the area summary.

description:
Read a document's structured data without changing it, including merged invalidity and diagnostics. Omit collection for an area summary with no schemas or values, or data: null when absent. Name a collection for its raw schema and a detached page in Unicode code-point id order; an unknown collection refuses. after is an exclusive cursor; ids optionally filters it and reports missing_ids. limit: 0 reads only the schema. max_bytes bounds canonical JSON of the page's id/value array, excluding schemas, diagnostics and formatting; a positive-limit page includes its first remaining record even over budget. It does not bound the whole response or token count. Follow next_after until complete; schema-only reads do not advance, and pages are not snapshots.

Help: get_data, workspaces, lifecycle, tool-contracts, data.

name: update_data
title: Update document data

schema.description: Raw versioned collection schema, validated by applyDocData.

description:
Apply one validated batch through applyDocData, naming each touched collection once. Within each collection, set `schema`, optionally `replaceRecords`, then `deleteRecords`, then `upsert` whole `{id, value}` records. `deleteCollection: true` excludes other changes. Schema and value JSON reach validation unaltered; unsupported schemas and invalid retained records refuse before mutation. The batch is one local transaction; identical refreshes return `changed: false` without an update. The result summarizes touched collection names, counts and deletion with durability, without values.

Refresh producer-owned collections by upsert or full-set replacement. Keep human dispositions in a separate collection keyed by producer record ids. Split changes above the 1 MiB schema/value budget across calls; they are not atomic together and supply no CAS or distributed lock. Read with get_data; get_doc summarizes collections. Decisions refuse data with decision_data_unsupported; decided records keep decision_read_only, and legacy data stays readable. Decision answer guidance is in lifecycle's Decision answers and topics section. Their directory answerPreview uses the first answer paragraph/list; decisions have no TL;DR. get_doc page decisions are marked related or linked. Recorded attribution {who, when, where} is separate from the answer's content blocks.

status.description: Only documents at this lifecycle state.

include_deleted.description: Include archived documents. Permanently deleted UUIDs are always excluded.

include_superseded.description: Return every decision record instead of one row per topic.

name: search
title: Search documents

query.description: Match any word in title, description, content or assigned tag names, including English word forms. Case and accents fold; `list_docs` matches adjacent `list docs`, and a trailing * matches stem prefixes. A prefix past the stem can miss: `decisi*` can miss `decision`; search the whole word or a shorter prefix, `decis*`. Results use title-weighted bm25 relevance.

limit.description: Maximum hits, from 1 to 100; defaults to 20 after filters.

tag.description: One catalog tag id or name (case ignored), or a nonempty list. Match any listed tag; carrying more listed tags boosts relevance. Unknown tags refuse.

kind.description: Only regular documents (including stored requirements) or decision records, including superseded, rejected and withdrawn records.

description:
Find live documents containing any query word in titles, descriptions, content or assigned tag names. English word forms match; case and accents fold, underscore groups match adjacent words and a trailing * matches stem prefixes. A prefix past the stem can miss: `decisi*` can miss `decision`; search the whole word or a shorter prefix, `decis*`. Punctuation or emoji alone matches nothing. Results use title-weighted bm25 relevance, without a strict title-first or matched-word-count order. Optional kind narrows to regular documents or decision records. Optional tag accepts one catalog id or current name (case ignored), or a list: any listed tag matches and more listed tags boost relevance; unknown tags refuse. Every hit includes kind and canonical tags; decision hits include current record state, including superseded and conflict. No hits does not prove the index is empty or the replica complete.

name: backlinks
title: Documents linking here
description:
Documents that reference this one, by UUID and never by path or title. The answer is the union of two kinds of edge, which it does not distinguish: the curated doc-level `links` set_metadata owns, and every inline reference in a prose block or table cell — written by link_range, an `inline` run, or a table cell's inline markdown. A citation needs no `links` entry to appear here.

Each one carries its `description` — null where it has none — so a citing document can be judged without opening it.

name: find_decisions
title: Find decisions linking a GitHub item

github_ref.description: One GitHub issue or pull request, as owner/repo#n or its github.com URL.

description:
Find live decision records whose prose links one GitHub issue or PR, using this replica's derived index without opening document rooms or calling GitHub. Only external link hrefs in prose count; labels, unlinked text and source blocks do not. Pass github_ref as owner/repo#n or an http(s) github.com /issues/n or /pull/n URL. Equivalent case/path spellings and suffixes normalize to the same identity; bare #n and other hosts refuse with invalid_github_reference. Returns every indexed live matching record once, ordered by title under SQLite binary collation then UUID, without pagination or topic resolution. Archived records are omitted. Results may lag unseen or unindexed content; an empty array does not prove replica completeness.

title: Edit one block

old_text.description: The block text you read. Asserted before the splice.

name: set_metadata
title: Set document metadata together

title.description: Display title. A decision topic has one title stored on its first record; title on any live record renames the topic without changing answer approval. Successors take the topic's title.

description.description: Agent-facing description used to choose whether to open the document.

tldr.description: Person-facing regular-document summary, at most 300 characters. Null clears it without changing a deliberate removal mark. On a marked page, a non-null summary requires tldr_opt_in: true. Decisions have no TL;DR; open records accept null.

tldr_opt_in.description: Pass true with a non-null tldr to lift a person's deliberate TL;DR removal. Requires a non-null tldr; false does not lift the mark.

discussion.description: RFC discussion document UUID, or null to clear. Only an open decision record accepts changes; the target must be live, locally readable and not a decision. Distinct from curated links and the recorded answer; no document is created or tagged.

code_check.description: Record a regular page's latest comparison for one repository, replacing only that repository's entry. The writer sets checked_at to current UTC; callers do not supply it. Content edits leave checks unchanged.

repository.description: Repository as owner/name; identity ignores letter case.

result.description: matches: page describes this code; ahead: intended behavior is missing; drift: unintended disagreement.

rev.description: Page rev read with get_doc and compared with code; must still be current.

paths.description: Literal repo-relative files/folders looked at; trailing / marks folders. No leading /, .. segments or globs. Duplicates removed; hints, not complete dependencies.

description:
Set title/description/tldr/tags/links/code_check or decision discussion; require one. Omissions stay; refusals write nothing and field failures name field. Title/description cannot be cleared. tldr: null clears but preserves deliberate absence; replacing a marked TL;DR requires tldr_opt_in: true with non-null tldr. Tags/links replace; [] clears. list_tags active ids/names (case ignored); assigned retired/unresolved ids stay. New links: directory-known; archived/unchanged accepted. Regular-only code_check replaces one repository's entry (case-insensitive); {repository, commit, result, rev, paths?}. rev must match get_doc's page rev; on refusal reread and compare before recording. paths are hints, not complete dependencies. Writer sets UTC checked_at. Content edits preserve checks; decisions refuse. Only open decisions accept discussion: live, readable non-decision RFC UUID/null. Reuse/create RFC first; RFC/page/approval untouched. Separate from curated links/recorded answer; fixed after open. Decisions have no TL;DR; non-null refuses decision_tldr_unsupported, open null accepted. Decided records refuse tldr/discussion. Title on any live record renames its decision topic; successors inherit it. Title renames preserve approval. answerPreview: first answer paragraph/list; get_doc marks related/linked. See lifecycle's Decision answers and topics section. Archived metadata refuses; lifecycle: set_status.

name: set_status
title: Set a document's lifecycle status

status.description: The recorded lifecycle state. Its kind owns the legal values.

when.description: When the person gave the answer, preferably an ISO date-time.

where.description: Where the answer was given, such as a conversation or review URL.

answer.description: Record a person's answer, not the agent's own approval. MCP does not verify its provenance.

reason.description: Non-empty reason required when rejecting a proposal.

description:
Record a document's lifecycle status. On an ordinary document this also adopts the kind that owns the status; the result names both, so adoption is never silent. A document that already has a kind accepts only that kind's statuses. Its kind is fixed through MCP: if it was adopted in error, retrying with the other kind's status cannot change it. An open record can be withdrawn without an answer; decided records cannot reopen or withdraw. Rejected and withdrawn are final. Rejection requires a non-empty `reason` and a recorded person's answer, and applies only to an open proposal, an agent stance or a decided record in a conflict. It stores `rejectionReason`. Validation refusals change nothing.

Help: set_status, workspaces, lifecycle, tool-contracts.

name: archive_doc
title: Archive a document
description:
Archive a document or every record in a decision topic: tombstone directory entries, drop local search rows and unconditionally unpin without erasing content. Reads by UUID remain available. unpinned reports the asserted unpin, not whether a pin was found. An unseen concurrent pin can survive with archived status; use get_sidebar then unpin_doc to remove it. This writes directory and sidebar rooms independently, without rollback or remote atomicity. The answer reports rooms; partial persistence_failed carries uuid, completed/failed rooms, rolledBack: false and recovery. Follow recovery to finish. indexed is false only on index-write failure; the archive remains applied and a later call retries indexing. Restoration uses restore_doc; pin_doc deliberately places the restored document back in navigation.

Help: archive_doc, workspaces, lifecycle, tool-contracts.

name: delete_doc
title: Permanently delete an archived document
description:
Permanently delete an archived regular document, including content, comments, data and history. Only its UUID and permanent deletion mark remain. Replicas remove their copies when they learn the mark; the hub refuses later room updates. This cannot be undone, including by an offline restore. Live documents refuse with doc_not_archived; deleted UUIDs refuse with doc_deleted; decision records refuse. Links stored in other documents stay unchanged. Directory and sidebar writes report independent durability.

Help: delete_doc, workspaces, lifecycle, tool-contracts.

name: restore_doc
title: Restore an archived document
description:
Remove one archive layer: restore an archived decision topic first, retaining records archived individually beforehand; in a live topic restore the addressed record. The archived result says whether that answer remains archived. Restore directory visibility and search indexing, using its recorded title and tags. It never restores a sidebar pin; use pin_doc for placement. On an already live regular document it can repair a drifted directory stub. Check indexed: false means this replica lacks the content or its index write failed. The restore still applies and replicates; search catches up when content arrives or a later call retries. Offline content arrival requires hub recovery.

Help: restore_doc, workspaces, lifecycle, tool-contracts.

column.description: Table cell column in the zero-based GFM projection.

oneOf.title: Opening a thread over a range

description:
Open a thread with block_id/start/end; reply with thread_id and no range fields; move an anchor with thread_id plus block_id/start/end. text adds a comment in every mode; author is optional. Only replies accept resolved to resolve or reopen. Moves remove all previous marks in the document and keep the thread's id, earlier replies and resolution, including for orphaned threads. Incomplete ranges refuse. Table targets need zero-based row/column GFM projection indices including header row 0. Offsets count displayed characters, including stored edge whitespace: remove exactly the GFM padding before decoding inline syntax. Coordinates follow moved cells; orphaned ranges are null. Bad or missing cell coordinates refuse with annotation_cell; empty or other-thread overlap ranges with annotation_range. Offsets clamp to text; a move may overlap its own anchor. Opening or moving into cards/Figma refuses with annotation_card/annotation_figma. Existing card/Figma threads accept replies, resolution, reopening or moves to prose/table cells; Figma ranges name caption.

name: link_range
title: Link a range of a block to another document

rev.description: The block's `rev` from get_doc. Required, and asserted.

description:
Mark selected prose text as a document reference without changing its characters or rev. start/end are character offsets measured against the required rev; stale_block returns currentText/currentRev for remeasurement. Indices clamp to text and swap if reversed; empty ranges refuse. Existing document references are retargeted; external links, source blocks, tables, cards and Figma blocks refuse. Write card and Figma caption links as inline Markdown in their container text. doc_id must be known to this replica's directory or doclink_target_not_known_locally refuses before writing; archived targets are accepted. The answer includes the target title, but the label stays the selected text and does not follow renames. Backlinks update without changing curated meta.links.

name: export_markdown
title: Export a document as markdown

frontmatter.description: Emit a YAML frontmatter block with uuid, title, tags and — when present — description, kind and status. The lifecycle fields record state; they do not authorize execution. Default true.

annotations.description: How to render annotation threads. Default drop.

description:
Render a Markdown projection: code, terminal and chart keep source fences; tables write padded GFM with inline cell marks. Cards export separate :::card containers with inline-Markdown prose and button: [Text](destination) lines after footer in authored order. Each exported button's plain label links to https or exact claude://code/new, claude-cli://open, codex://new, optionally with ?query. Style outline/filled and color neutral/blue/green/violet default to outline neutral; export writes style before color and omits defaults. Import restores buttons and appearances. Figma exports separate :::figma containers: url, optional literal title and height, blank line and marked caption. Normalized HTTPS www.figma.com links retain design/file/proto/board/slides/community/file path, key/id, optional name and node-id, starting-point-node-id, version-id; other query values and fragments were dropped at save. Absent keys are omitted; header newlines fold to spaces and prose lines starting ::: are escaped. Import restores caption marks and adjacent containers; invalid/unclosed containers remain literal paragraphs. MCP refuses bad Figma content with invalid_figma; get_doc derives kind/file/fileName/node. Markdown help owns height 240–960 and accepted links. Export contacts no Figma service. Chart/data records are omitted with a notice; Markdown is never storage and MCP has no import tool.

Help: export_markdown, workspaces, lifecycle, tool-contracts, markdown, data.

name: sync_status
title: Sync status
description:
Inspect local replica state, pending rooms and hub connection/acknowledgements. hub.status distinguishes disabled, retryable hub-down, auth-failed requiring action, and update-required protocol mismatch. hub.recoveryClass, authRecovery and reason explain recovery; protocolVersion and hubProtocolVersion identify the incompatible side. Tools still work locally. unsyncedChanges counts durable pending rooms; inFlightUpdates counts provider sync messages on the current connection, resetting on reconnect. lastSync is this machine's stored UTC time when its full replica caught up, or null; it never moves backwards across processes. persistence diagnoses a failed log append and remains readable when ordinary replica tools are quarantined until restart. See this tool's help for counter units and lastSync conditions.

Help: sync_status, workspaces, tool-contracts.

name: get_sidebar
title: Read the sidebar
description:
The workspace's curated navigation: named groups of pinned documents, in the order they are stored. This is not the corpus — unpinned documents are fully alive and reachable through list_docs, search, links and backlinks. Unpinned documents are simply not entry points.

Help: get_sidebar, workspaces, lifecycle, tool-contracts.

name: pin_doc
title: Pin a document into a sidebar group

group.description: Group name, or the group id get_sidebar returned.

index.description: Position, clamped into range. Omitted means last.

description:
Pin a document into a group, creating the group when no group carries that name. `index` places it; omit it to append.

One pin per document across the whole sidebar, so this is also how a pinned document is moved or reordered: pinning one that is already pinned moves it to `index` in the named group — carrying the pin as it stands rather than re-pinning it, so a concurrent unpin still wins — and `index` then counts positions in the target group after the document has been taken out of it.

Help: pin_doc, workspaces, lifecycle, tool-contracts.

name: unpin_doc
title: Unpin a document
description:
Remove a document from the sidebar, wherever it sits. The document itself is untouched: unpinning is a navigation act. archive_doc hides a document; delete_doc permanently deletes an archived regular document.

An unpin beats a move made concurrently on another replica, so a document does not reappear because somebody was dragging it at the time. It takes no group: one pin per document means there is only ever one place to remove it from. `unpinned` is false when the document was not pinned to begin with.

Help: unpin_doc, workspaces, lifecycle, tool-contracts.

name: sidebar_group
title: Rename, delete or move a sidebar group

action.description: What to do with the group.

group.description: Group name, or the group id get_sidebar returned.

name.description: The new name. rename only, and required there.

index.description: Position, clamped into range. Omitted means last.

description:
Manage the groups themselves. `delete` removes the group and its pins — the documents are untouched, because the group only ever held their uuids, and they stay reachable through list_docs and search.

`action` picks one of three shapes and each takes only its own field: `rename` needs `name` and refuses `index`, `move` takes `index` (omitted: last) and refuses `name`, `delete` takes neither. A field belonging to another action is refused at the input boundary before the sidebar is touched, rather than ignored — so a call that says two things is a failure you can see, not a silent half-success.

There is no create action: pin_doc creates a group by naming one that does not exist, which is how a group comes into being with something in it rather than empty.

Help: sidebar_group, workspaces, lifecycle, tool-contracts.

name: get_help
title: Read product help

topic.description: Help topic id or exact registered tool name. Omit to list all topics.

description:
Read bundled, version-matched product help by topic or exact registered tool name. Omit topic to list every topic with its id, title, description and URI. The returned text is the same Markdown as uberblick://help/{topic}. Help is workspace-agnostic, needs no guidance briefing and never opens or settles a replica; it remains available offline and while the replica store is quarantined. Unknown topics refuse with unknown_help_topic and list valid topic ids; choose one and retry.

Help: get_help, orientation, tools, tool-contracts.
